decks.title: Quality Gates for AI-Generated Software
decks.desc: The four-gate release discipline behind 30+ shipped apps: golden path, zero dead buttons, version-and-backup, and physical evidence - with one rule: a blocker stops the line.
decks.subtitle: Speed without gates is debt at machine pace

slides.title: Quality gates for AI-generated software
slides.note: The release discipline behind 30+ production apps · Rezalian Vatiady

slides.title: AI writes code at machine speed
bullets: Unreviewed speed is technical debt at machine pace
The failure mode is subtle: a button that does nothing
Silent skips, unbumped versions, flows that lie
Gates turn speed from a liability into an asset

slides.title: The golden path must work
bullets: One most-important user journey per app
Walked end-to-end every release, no exceptions
If it breaks, nothing else matters - the build stops
Boring, repeatable, non-negotiable

slides.title: Zero dead buttons
bullets: Every interactive element does what it claims or gets removed
Agents sweep every screen systematically
An element that lies is a bug, full stop
Offline behavior gets checked too

slides.title: Version bump plus backup
bullets: No release without a version increment
The previous version is archived before the new one ships
Rollback is a normal procedure, not an emergency
This rule has saved more projects than any architecture

slides.title: Physical evidence
bullets: Passing means a log, file, screenshot, or marker
Something a stranger could audit
A status field is not evidence
Agents behave differently when proof is mandatory

slides.title: A gate that cannot stop traffic is not a gate
bullets: One blocked item = no deploy
No 'just this once' - that is how gates die
Evidence recorded where reviewers can find it

slides.title: Make honesty cheaper than lying
slides.note: Design the system so the easy path and the correct path are the same path. · rezalianvatiady.github.io

decks.title: The ETL Playbook: Data Quality at Scale
decks.desc: Five principles for pipelines that stay trustworthy: profile sources, reconcile at the seams, instrument the schedule, give discrepancies owners, and document where the work happens.
decks.subtitle: ETL fails quietly - unless you design against it

slides.title: The ETL playbook
slides.note: Lessons from retail BI across four countries and the frameworks that followed · Rezalian Vatiady

slides.title: ETL fails quietly
bullets: Silent truncation, schema drift, stale schedules
Nobody notices for weeks - then leadership quotes the wrong number
The pipeline that 'works' is the most dangerous one
Design against quiet failure, not loud failure

slides.title: Profile sources before you trust them
bullets: Expected row counts, key uniqueness, update cadence
Known quirks documented per source
Restated numbers, skipped weekends - every source has a personality
Half of quality issues are undocumented source behavior

slides.title: Reconcile at the seams
bullets: Every boundary crossing gets reconciliation checks
Row counts, sum checks, sampled row-level comparisons
Every load - not quarterly, not on request
Reconciliation is a property of the pipeline, not a project

slides.title: Instrument the schedule itself
bullets: Freshness alarms on every source
If data is late, someone hears before the CEO does
Schedule deaths caused more incidents than logic bugs
Silent is the default state - fight it on purpose

slides.title: Discrepancies get owners
bullets: A mismatch between systems is an organizational fact
Named owners on both sides, not just a ticket
Data quality is a relationship between teams

slides.title: Document where the work happens
bullets: Runbooks next to the pipelines, not in a forgotten wiki
Pipeline maps, ownership, decisions logged
The quirk you document today is the incident you prevent next month

slides.title: Trust is built one reconciliation at a time
slides.note: And destroyed by one unexplained number. · rezalianvatiady.github.io
